title: Dimension drop for a bad locus under a finite morphism
statement:
Let $V$ be a Noetherian scheme of finite topological Krull dimension, and let $A\subseteq |V|$ be a set of points. Assume the following generic spreading condition: for every integral reduced closed subscheme $T\subseteq V$ with generic point $\xi\notin A$, there is a nonempty open subset of $T$ disjoint from $A$. Put $Z=\overline A$, with its reduced closed subscheme structure. Every generic point of an irreducible component of $Z$ belongs to $A$, and there are only finitely many such points.
Moreover, let $a:W\to V$ be a finite morphism with $W$ Noetherian, and let $A_W\subseteq |W|$ satisfy the same generic spreading condition on integral reduced closed subschemes of $W$. Suppose $A_W\subseteq a^{-1}(A)$ and suppose that, for every generic point $s$ of an irreducible component of $Z$, one has $A_W\cap a^{-1}(s)=\varnothing$. Put $Z_W=\overline{A_W}$ with its reduced closed structure. Then
$$ Z_W\subseteq a^{-1}(Z),\qquad Z_W\cap a^{-1}(s)=\varnothing\quad\text{for every such }s. $$
If $Z$ is nonempty of dimension $d$, every strict specialization chain in $Z_W$ has length less than $d$; consequently $Z_W$ is empty for $d=0$, and for nonempty $Z_W$ one has $\dim Z_W<\dim Z$. If $Z$ is empty, then $Z_W$ is empty. The finite morphism need not be flat, surjective, or generically etale.

Schemes, finite morphisms, integral schemes, generic points, closed and open subschemes, and irreducible components use [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-sc-generic-point], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-open-immersion] and [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact. The bar denotes topological closure; $x$ specializes to $y$ when $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$. Dimension is the supremum of the lengths of strict specialization chains [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The reduced induced closed structures are those of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme].

proof.text: For either $(X,B)=(V,A)$ or $(W,A_W)$, put $E=\overline B$. The reduced induced closed structure on $E$, and on each closed irreducible subset of $E$, exists by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Since $X$ is Noetherian, [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] writes $E=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_r$ as its finitely many distinct irreducible components. Each $C_i$ has a unique generic point $\eta_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], applied to the closed irreducible subset $C_i$ of $X$. Its reduced closed structure is integral: it is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, exactly the equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. These are therefore legitimate test subschemes for the assumed spreading condition. The case $E=\varnothing$ has $r=0$.

proof.text:
Fix $i$. If $\eta_i
otin B$, spreading supplies a nonempty relatively open $O\subseteq C_i$ disjoint from $B$. Every nonempty open in $C_i$ contains $\eta_i$: if it missed $\eta_i$, its closed complement would contain $\overline{\{\eta_i\}}=C_i$. Also $\eta_i
otin C_j$ for $j
e i$, since otherwise $C_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}\subseteq C_j$, contradicting distinct maximal components. Thus $D=E\setminus igcup_{j
e i}C_j$ is an open neighbourhood of $\eta_i$ in $E$, contained in $C_i$. Write $O=C_i\cap H$ for $H$ open in $E$. Then $D\cap H$ is a nonempty open in $E$ disjoint from $B$, contrary to $E=\overline B$. Indeed any such open is $E\cap H'$ with $H'$ ambient open meeting $E$; by the definition of closure $H'$ meets $B\subseteq E$. Hence every $\eta_i\in B$. Applying this to $V$ gives the first assertion, including finiteness, and applying it to $W$ gives the same assertion for $Z_W$.

proof.text: The underlying map of the scheme morphism $a$ is continuous. Since $Z$ is closed, $a^{-1}(Z)$ is closed and contains $A_W\subseteq a^{-1}(A)\subseteq a^{-1}(Z)$. Taking closures yields $Z_W\subseteq a^{-1}(Z)$. In particular $Z=\varnothing$ forces $A_W=Z_W=\varnothing$.

source.place: Definition 01IJ (definition-scheme); elementary continuity/closure argument for de Jong Lemma 5.7, p.615, containment of the new bad closure over the old one.

proof.text: Suppose $w\in Z_W$ and $a(w)=s$, where $s$ is the generic point of a component $C$ of $Z$. Choose a component of $Z_W$ containing $w$ (step 1), and let $t$ be its generic point. Step 2 gives $t\in A_W$. Continuity implies that $x=a(t)$ specializes to $s$, while step 3 gives $x\in Z$. The irreducible closed set $\overline{\{x\}}\subseteq Z$ contains $s$ and hence contains $\overline{\{s\}}=C$. Maximality of $C$ forces $\overline{\{x\}}=C$; uniqueness of its generic point gives $x=s$. (The closure of a singleton is irreducible because any two opens meeting it both contain that point.) Consequently $t\in A_W\cap a^{-1}(s)$, contradicting the assumed emptiness. This proves $Z_W\cap a^{-1}(s)=\varnothing$ for every old component generic point. Notice that this step needs no flatness or surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober), with topology.tex Tags 004V and 004X; elementary generic-point argument filling de Jong Lemma 5.7, p.615, assertion that the new bad closure avoids the old maximal points.

proof.text: A strict specialization $u\rightsquigarrow v$ in $W$ remains strict after applying $a$. Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $a(v)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. It also contains $a(u)$: an open containing a specialization contains its generalization. Finiteness in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] identifies $a^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $S$ a finite $R$-module. The points $u,v$ correspond to primes $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak q'$ of $S$: in the Zariski topology $\overline{\{\mathfrak q\}}=V(\mathfrak q)$, because a closed set $V(I)$ contains $\mathfrak q$ exactly when $I\subseteq\mathfrak q$. The map on points is contraction for the ring map $R\to S$ of [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] this map is integral, and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] gives $\mathfrak q\cap R\subsetneq\mathfrak q'\cap R$. Thus $a(u)\ne a(v)$. Continuity already gives specialization, proving the claim for each adjacent pair in any chain.

source.place: Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion); schemes.tex Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens), morphisms.tex Tag 01WH. Affine strict-contraction justification of de Jong Lemma 5.7, p.615, finite-map dimension comparison.

proof.text: Let $w_0\rightsquigarrow\cdots\rightsquigarrow w_n$ be a strict chain in $Z_W$. Its image $x_0\rightsquigarrow\cdots\rightsquigarrow x_n$ is strict by step 5 and lies in $Z$ by step 3. Choose a component $C$ of $Z$ containing $x_0$ and its generic point $s$. Then $s$ specializes to $x_0$, and $s\ne x_0$ by step 4. Prepending $s$ gives a strict chain of length $n+1$ in $Z$. To compare with [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], in a closed subset of a scheme chains of irreducible closed sets correspond, in reverse order, to strict specialization chains: choose the unique generic point of each closed set using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]; conversely send a point to its singleton closure. Inclusion of closures is specialization and equality forces equality of their generic points. Thus $n+1\le d=\dim Z$, so $n<d$. The dimension of $Z$ is finite since its closed-set chains are also chains in $V$. If $d=0$, even a chain consisting of one point would give $1\le0$, so $Z_W=\varnothing$. Otherwise all chain lengths in a nonempty $Z_W$ lie in $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ and their supremum is at most $d-1<d$. Together with step 3 this proves every dimension and empty-case assertion.
